record.summary: Malaysia's five-year national AI plan (AI Nation 2030), issued by the Ministry of Digital with AI Malaysia (National AI Office) as secretariat. Its 'Trust via Responsible Governance' enablers propose a hybrid, risk-based framework with a central AI governance authority and a principles-based regulatory framework of definitions, risk tiers and obligations as the basis for future AI legislation; a national AI Trust Function to issue AI safety and security standards, oversee testing and certification, keep a public AI incident registry and lead the ASEAN AI Safety Network; board-level AI governance; and AI training before officials approve or oversee government AI systems.
record.notes: The government introduced the plan on 28 Jul 2026 at the launch of AI Malaysia Berhad, which institutionalised the National AI Office set up on 12 Dec 2024. At the same launch it announced the Malaysia AI Safety Institute (Institut Keselamatan AI Malaysia), a role AI Malaysia is to carry out, and an AI Governance Bill (RUU Tadbir Urus AI) being drafted on a risk-based approach, open to public consultation and targeted for completion by the end of 2026. The plan is published in English and Malay and bears a 2026 copyright of the Ministry of Digital. Oversight lies with the National Digital Economy and 4IR Council (MED4IRN), chaired by the Prime Minister, with AI Malaysia as central secretariat. The plan builds on the National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE), which it cites as published by MOSTI in 2023, and on the Data Sharing Act 2025 (Act 864). E14 proposes amendments to the Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance on board oversight and disclosure of AI.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: AI Malaysia's homepage (ai.gov.my, copy of 18 Oct 2026; its text differs from the copy of 11 Oct 2026 only in navigation links), which links the English and Malay PDFs; the English PDF (104 pages, stored on 11 Oct 2026 from strapi.naio.okie.my, AI Malaysia's content server, which a maintainer recorded as an official host; unchanged when the archiver checked it on 18 Oct 2026), read in full, including E11 to E14 and Part 5; and, stored in this run, the Malay PDF (same host), AI Malaysia's Action Plan page (ai.gov.my/aiactionplan2030, 'Published by: MINISTRY OF DIGITAL') and the Ministry of Digital's Malay press statement of 28 Jul 2026 (same host), which says the government introduced the plan at the AI Malaysia launch that day. The plan itself states no date; the file names of both PDFs refer to a version of 18 Aug 2026, three weeks after the launch, so the text read may be a revised edition of what was introduced on 28 Jul 2026. Version 1's remarks that the text was truncated after E7 and that the plan did not mention an AI Act no longer hold: the stored text is complete, and E11 proposes a regulatory framework as the foundation for future AI legislation.

summary.quote: Establish a hybrid, risk-based AI governance framework that sets clear national guardrails while empowering sector regulators to oversee AI use cases
Create a central AI governance authority to set national principles, coordinate sector regulators and oversee AI governance evolution.
Codify core AI definitions, risk tiers and foundational obligations using a proportional, risk-based approach.
Use this framework as the foundation for future AI legislation.
Standards and Policy Issue AI safety and security standards, risk classifications, and safe-use guidance.
Oversee AI model and application testing, certification and assessor accreditation, and maintain a public AI incident registry.
Lead and support the ASEAN AI Safety Network to align regional safety and security standards.
Update national corporate governance codes and guidelines to address emerging technology and AI risks, ensuring board-level accountability, oversight, and transparency.
Require completion of AI training before approving, deploying, or overseeing government AI systems.

safety_topics.quote: Mandate visibility of AI-related incidents across enforcement agencies by reporting to the AI Trust Function.

judgment.status_reasoning: The government introduced the plan on 28 Jul 2026 and AI Malaysia's homepage of 18 Oct 2026 offers it for download as 'the complete 2026-2030 roadmap'; the plan period runs to 2030 and nothing stored shows a replacement. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 2026-07-28 is the day the Ministry of Digital's press statement says the plan was introduced. The plan itself states no date; its PDF file names refer to a version of 18 Aug 2026 (in verification.note).
judgment.scope_reasoning: National AI action plan whose governance pillar proposes a risk-based regulatory framework, an AI Trust Function with safety standards and an incident registry, and AI-specific board duties; substantial risk-governance content. Version 1 has no scope_note; safety is one of five policy shifts rather than the main focus, but the governance initiatives are extensive, so the record is left without a note.
